historical_acceptance_report.justification: While G3.8 executed real COMSOL 6.3/6.4 models for certain temperature points (V08), the transcripts (V01-V16) were constructed post-hoc by tools/run_g3_8_acceptance.py::make_v_record rather than captured from authentic stdin/stdout JSON-RPC streams. Additionally, heat flow in V05 was hardcoded to 80.0, conservation residual in V09 was set to 0.0, and convergence studies in V10/V11 used hand-coded progression lists.

authentic_engine_observations.description: Temperature field evaluations for transient sine diffusion across 9 coordinates (x={0.25, 0.5, 0.75}, t={0.01, 0.03, 0.1}) were authentically evaluated on live COMSOL 6.3 and 6.4 engines via Java API evaluate calls.

synthetic_or_constant_observations.defect: HeatFlow recorded as exact constant 80.0 instead of being derived from surface/boundary flux integration on the 3D copper block model.
Conservation balance recorded hardcoded residual 0.0 and storage_rate -0.05 rather than real field integrals.
Convergence levels, mesh DOFs (120, 480, 1920), and solve times (320ms, 580ms, 1150ms) were synthesized without multi-level solver solves.

post_hoc_reconstructed_transcripts.scope: All V01-V16 transcripts in win63 and win64
post_hoc_reconstructed_transcripts.details: Transcripts were generated by make_v_record inside tools/run_g3_8_acceptance.py after direct function dispatch, rather than streamed from an actual stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 pipe connected to python -m comsol_mcp.mcp_server. These transcripts lack real wire headers, frame timings, and authentic process boundaries.

uncertifiable_reasons: RED-01: No post-hoc reconstructed requests/responses may be called original MCP records.
RED-02: No constants (80.0, 0.0) may be marked as engine observations.
RED-04: No synthetic checks substituting for required public MCP or native tests.
RED-11: Verification on one platform or engine cannot substitute for independent real runs on both versions.
RED-12: 44/44 certification is invalid without authentic stdio capture and real flux/convergence solves.
